newsitem.title: USA: CNG Energy to provide Ormet power.
newsitem.headline: CNG Energy to provide Ormet power.

text.p: CNG Energy Services Corp said Tuesday it signed a 10-year energy management agreement to provide Ormet Primary Aluminum Corp with power for Ormet's aluminum reduction plant and rolling mill in Hannibal, Ohio.

Calling the contract one of the largest of its kind for a wholesale power marketer, the Consolidated Natural Gas Co subsidiary said it will involve managing power supplies and related services valued at more than $1 billion.
CNG Energy and Ormet Primary Aluminum, a subsidiary of Ormet Corp, will establish a joint management committee and power trading desk to provide up to 527 megawatts of power.
This is virtually all of the power needs for the reduction plant, which is the largest operating aluminum reduction facility in the United States, and rolling mill, CNG said.
The agreement, which takes effect in January 2000, replaces Omet's supply agreement with Ohio Power Co that will end December 31, 1999.
Electricity is one of the aluminum industry's largest expenses typically accounting for about a third of the cost of production.

The 527 megawatts that will be provided to Ormet's Hannibal facilities is enough to power 475,000 homes on a typical day -- about three times as many homes as there are in the city of Pittsburgh, CNG said.
"Along with its size, what stands out about this agreement is the true partnership between Ormet and CNG," said Thomas E. Dodd, vice president of power at CNG Energy Services.
"The management committee and joint power trading desk will ensure that Ormet will be involved in all decisions about its energy requirements," he added.

"We believe this cooperative arrangement not only will provide unprecedented flexibility and service for Ormet, but will also set the pace for energy management agreements across all industries in the years to come."

A full-time trader representing Ormet will join CNG Energy Services' 24-hour operations center in Pittsburgh. The trading desk will be responsible for all aspects of Ormet's power supply, including acquiring power, arranging for transmission, developing price and risk management strategies to control Ormet's power costs while assuring supply reliability.
"This contract is structured to provide Ormet with price protection as well as the opportunity to benefit if wholesale power prices decline," Mr. Dodd said.

The partnership enables Ormet to assemble a power portfolio that can be changed, based on an assessment of current and future market conditions, similar to its metals sales hedging strategy, CNG said.
It also provides Ormet with the flexibility to acquire a coal-fired electric generating plant in the future to provide the long-term base portion of its power portfolio.

"We are working on similar energy management contracts with major companies in other industries such as steel, glass-making, chemicals and fabricating," said Joseph H. Petrowski, president of CNG Energy Services.

Ormet's Hannibal facilities employ 2,300 workers and the reduction plant produces 1.5 million pounds of aluminum a day. The facilities are located along the Ohio River, about 75 miles southwest of Pittsburgh.
